definitions.explanation: A person or business that installs and repairs water pipes, faucets, and plumbing fixtures.

examples.japanese: {水道屋|すいどうや}を{呼|よ}んだ。
{水漏|みずも}れがひどいので、{水道屋|すいどうや}に{修理|しゅうり}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: The water leak was bad, so I asked a plumber to fix it.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{水道屋|すいどうや}さんに{蛇口|じゃぐち}の{交換|こうかん}を{依頼|いらい}したら、すぐに{来|き}てくれた。
examples.english: When I asked the neighborhood plumber to replace the faucet, they came right away.

notes:
An everyday word for a plumber or plumbing service. Composed of {水道|すいどう} (water supply, plumbing) + {屋|や} (shop, dealer, person in a trade). The suffix {屋|や} is commonly used for tradespeople and shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水道屋|すいどうや}を{呼|よ}ぶ: to call a plumber
- {水道屋|すいどうや}に{頼|たの}む: to ask a plumber
- {水道屋|すいどうや}さん: plumber (polite, with さん)

THE ～{屋|や} PATTERN:
Many tradespeople and shops use this suffix:
- {電気屋|でんきや}: electrician; electronics store
- {大工|だいく}: carpenter (does not use {屋|や})
- ガス{屋|や}: gas company/worker
- {引越|ひっこ}し{屋|や}: moving company

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {配管工|はいかんこう}: plumber — more formal/technical term for the tradesperson
- {水道工事|すいどうこうじ}: plumbing work — refers to the work itself
- {水道局|すいどうきょく}: water department — the municipal water authority
